paper.title: Reward Maximization Under Uncertainty: Leveraging Side-Observations on Networks

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic MAB with side-observations on a bipartite action/base-arm network
unmapped: Feedback is given by a known bipartite graph between K actions and N base-arms (unknowns): playing action j reveals samples of all base-arms in V_j; reward of action j is a known bounded function f_j of base-arms K_j ⊆ V_j
N here denotes the number of base-arms, not agents
Regret bounds expressed via optimal value of the hitting-set LP relaxation P2
settings.definition_quote: Let $\mathcal{N}=\{1,\ldots,N\}$ denote the collection of {\it base-arms} with unknown distributions. Subsets of base-arms form {\it actions}, and are indexed by $\mathcal{K}=\{1,\ldots,K\}$. ... When the decision maker chooses action $j$ at time $t$, he or she observes one realization for each of the random variables $X_i(t)$, $i\in V_j$. ... We assume that the reward is bounded in $[0,1]$ for each action.

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic MAB with side-observations on a bipartite network (lower bound)
unmapped: Known bipartite graph between actions and base-arms determines side observations; base-arm distributions belong to a parametric density family g(x;theta) satisfying Lai-Robbins regularity (finiteness, continuity, denseness)
settings.definition_quote: Let the probability distribution $F_{i}$ have a univariate density function $g(x;\theta_{i})$ with unknown parameters $\theta_{i}$, for each $i\in\mathcal{N}$.

symbols.c_mu: optimal value of LP P1: min sum_{j in U} Delta_j w_j s.t. sum_{j in S_i} w_j >= 1/J_i(theta_i) for all base-arms i, w >= 0

conditions: Assumptions 1-3 (finiteness, continuity, denseness of KL) on base-arm densities

source.label: prop:lbSO

Then, under any uniformly good policy $\bm{\phi},$ the expected regret is asymptotically bounded below as follows: \liminf_{t\rightarrow\infty}\frac{R_{\bm{\mu}}(t)}{\log(t)}\ge c_{\bm{\mu}}, where $c_{\bm{\mu}}$ is the optimal value of the following linear program (LP) $P_{1}$

results.notes: Derived from Lai-Robbins Theorem 2. Proposition 6 relates c_mu to the LP P2 value sum z_j^* (not recorded separately).

symbols.z_i: optimal solution z_j^* of the hitting-set LP relaxation P2 for action j
symbols.d_alg: algorithm parameter d with 0 < d < min gap
symbols.lambda_K: max_j |K_j|, max number of base-arms in an action's reward
symbols.delta_S: max_i |S_i|, maximum support degree of base-arms

tuning: c > max(2 alpha d^2 / r, 4 alpha) for some alpha > 1

source.label: prop:epsgreedyk
source.quote: Choose parameters $c$ and $d$ such that, $0<d<\min_{j\in\cU}\Delta_{j},$ and $c>\max(2 \alpha d^{2}/r,4\alpha),$ for any $\alpha>1.$ Then, the expected regret at time $T$ of the $\epsilon_{t}$-greedy-LP policy ... is at most \left(\frac{c}{d^{2}}\sum_{j\in\cU}\Delta_{j}z_{j}^{*}\right)\log(T)+O(K), ... In particular, the $O(K)$ term is at most ...

results.notes: Built on Proposition 7 (per-round probability of selecting a suboptimal action, not recorded separately). Requires d below the minimum gap (Delta_lower_bound). Does not need T.

symbols.z_i: optimal solution z_j^* of LP P2
symbols.b_i: indicator that suboptimal action j belongs to the set B = {j in U: m_j > m_bar}
symbols.Deltahat_i: max{2^{-m_bar+2}, min_{a: j in G_a} Delta_a}

source.label: prop:ucblp
source.quote: Then, the expected regret due to the UCB-LP policy described in Algorithm~\ref{alg:ucblp} is at most \sum_{j\in \cU\setminus B} \Delta_{j} z_{j}^{*}\frac{32\log(T\hat{\Delta}_{j}^{2})}{\hat{\Delta}_{j}^{2}} + \sum_{j\in B} \frac{32\log(T\Delta_{j}^{2})}{\Delta_{j}}+O(K^{2}),

results.notes: Leading terms have explicit constants; only the K^2 term is O(.), so notation O covers the whole expression. Indicator symbols used to encode sums over B and U\B.

symbols.Z_star: optimal value sum_j z_j^* of LP P2 (LP relaxation of minimum hitting set)

conditions: Assumption 4: |O| (number of optimal actions), min gap, and min_i J_i(theta_i) are constants independent of K and N

source.label: prop:ucblp
source.quote: Further, under Assumption~\ref{assum:bounded}, the regret is also at most O\left(\sum_{j\in\cK}z_{j}^{*}\log(T)\right) + O(K^{2}), where $(z_{j}^{*})$ entirely captures the time dependence on network structure.

source.label: app:unknown
source.quote: When the horizon is unknown, start the UCB-LP algorithm with $\tilde{T}_0=2$ and increase $\tilde{T}$ after reaching $\tilde{T}$ steps by setting $\tilde{T}_{l+1}=\tilde{T}_l^2.$ The regret of unknown horizon UCB-LP is bounded by \sum_{j\in \cU\setminus B}\frac{64\Delta_{j} z_{j}^{*}}{\hat{\Delta}_{j}^{2}} \log(T\hat{\Delta}_{j}^{2})+\sum_{j\in B} \frac{64\log(T\Delta_{j}^{2})}{\Delta_{j}}+O(K^2\log_2\log_2 T).

results.notes: log_2 log_2 T written as log(log(T)) under O. Setting s1 lists T as known for UCB-LP; this variant does not need T.
